conclusion: No, not with rules we can actually apply. As oracles the three do add up to more than +0.01, but realistic versions capture about 3% of that. Measured on the exp60 ins35 bed (56 clips, official metric; base 0.93988, div 25/31/74 reproduced; GT never used to decide an edit). ORACLES: joint F + L + O with the round-11 definitions = +0.0135 (44b6 +0.0070, 6bba +0.0139; clip-bootstrap 90% +0.0089..+0.0187), more than the sum 0.0063 + 0.0054 + 0.0001 = 0.0118, because removing FP forks and adding TP forks compound in the division Jaccard. With a perfect filter on the wide orphan pool (20 TP forks) the joint oracle is +0.0271. (The sibling m_joint_oracle.json, whose relink oracle includes swaps, gets +0.0206.) REALISTIC: best combination = forkmid 4.5 um -> flow-compensated end->free-start link R 8 um -> mirror orphan attach residual <= 1.0 um. Each knob was picked in-sample from a 3-point grid, so this is optimistic. Result: +0.00039 pooled (44b6 0.00000, 6bba +0.00041); 3 clips win and 2 lose; clip-bootstrap 90% [-0.0008, +0.0020]. Almost all of it is one recovered division in one clip (6bba_debd7bfa +0.028). The pre-declared middle setting (forkmid 4.5, R 5, residual 1.5) is NEGATIVE: -0.00038 (44b6 -0.0025; 5 clips win, 9 lose). Per family: (1) Fork removal: best +0.00017 (forkmid 4.5 removes 1 FP fork, 0 TP, 39 metric-ignored = 2.7% of the +0.0063 oracle). Every other grid point is <= 0: ANTIPAR -0.0001..-0.0008, any-fork midpoint 4.5 um -0.0037 (removes 5 TP forks). (2) Orphan attach: best +0.00020 at residual 1.0 (new forks 1 TP / 4 FP = 20% evaluable precision). Residual 1.5: 2/13 = 13%, -0.0005. Residual 3.0: 7/200 = 3.4%, -0.0129. Break-even precision is ~26.5%. (3) Linking: +0.00002. The t+1 end->free-start pool is empty below ~8 um because the ILP already links everything closer; R 8 makes 8 links in 56 clips, 1 TP. Gap closing t->t+2 with an interpolated node gives 0 TP and is slightly negative. Most edits the rules can make without GT land on unannotated cells (metric-ignored), and the evaluable ones are <= 20% precise. At the observed ~1/6 lab-to-public transfer, +0.00039 lab is ~+0.00007 public, against the R4 bar of +0.002 public (~+0.012 lab), so ~30x short. Answer: a realistic combination is barely positive in-sample at its best grid point, but it is noise-level, driven by one clip, negative at the pre-declared setting, and far below the bar. The line stays closed. Not measured here: a realistic swap/relink rule (the part of the sibling's link oracle that comes from swaps). The nearest measured realistic analogue, RE-AIM, was a no-op.
